messages:
maria_support: FYI — Customer AcmeCorp (org=acme, proj=prod) reported a burst of 429s around 2026-03-15T09:02Z while the quota dashboard shows ~40% available for the project. They hit throttles and app degraded. Can someone look?

kevin_eng: can you paste a sample request_id + header snapshot? also which quota tile they were looking at (project vs org)?

maria_support: request-ids: rq_01H9X2B4, rq_01H9X2F9. Headers: 
```
x-project-id: prod
x-org-id: acme
x-request-id: rq_01H9X2B4
authorization: Bearer <redacted>
```
Dashboard screenshot attached showed "Project quota (1h rolling): used 600k / 1.5M" but they saw 429s for many short requests.

sre-bot: alert: rate_limit_spike org=acme projects: prod, staging — spike detected 2026-03-15T09:01:50Z -> 09:04:10Z. Avg token/sec doubled.

kevin_eng: quick check — can you paste a short example of a request that got 429 (body or tokens)? need to reproduce locally to see if metering increment mismatch or enforcement bug.

maria_support: got a minimal repro from customer: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Body {"prompt":"short"}
Response 429 {"error":"rate_limit","details":"project token window exceeded"}
```
They sent many ~20-50 req/s bursts across a handful of API keys.

olivia_billing: invoices for acme show no unexpected billing delta in that hour — token counts on billing pipeline match expected. So likely enforcement vs dashboard mismatch (metering vs enforcement).

anna_analytics: I ran the tile aggregation query for the 1h rolling tile. Query (simplified):
```
-- compute rolling token count per tile
SELECT tile_key, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM token_events
WHERE ts >= '2026-03-15 08:00:00' AND ts < '2026-03-15 10:00:00'
GROUP BY tile_key;
```
I compared project-level tiles and org-level aggregates and I see overlapping counts for events that have both project_id and org_id attributes — when we aggregate by org we were summing both project tiles and org-wide tiles in some shards. Looks like double-counts for ~12% of events during the spike window.

kevin_eng: that smells like a sharding/tiling alignment issue. Our enforcement path reads the rolling window by looking up pre-aggregated tiles keyed by (shard_id, bucket_ts). If the dashboard query uses a different shard key (org_id) it may be summing two distinct tile sets. Can you run the following to confirm?
```
-- compare raw events -> tiles -> enforcement read
SELECT e.event_id, e.ts, e.tokens, t.tile_key
FROM token_events e
LEFT JOIN token_tiles t ON (e.shard = t.shard AND floor(e.ts/60) = t.bucket_minute)
WHERE e.org_id = 'acme' AND e.ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15 09:00:00' AND '2026-03-15 09:10:00';
```

anna_analytics: ran it. For ~700 events the join returned two different tile_key rows (project_tile AND org_tile) for the same event_id in different shards — and enforcement reads from project_tile only, while dashboard sums both sets when org-aggregation is requested.

ryan_pm: quick question — why would the dashboard sum both? I thought we deduplicate at render time.

kevin_eng: supposed to dedupe, but we discovered a TTL mismatch on the event dedup table vs tile ingestion. Sequence: events are ingested -> tile writer writes per-project tiles (shard by project) and also emits org-tiles (shard by org). Dedup tokens are kept for 30s in ingestion to avoid double-write. During heavy bursts the tile writer retried and tombstoned some events causing them to be written into the second shard on retry. The dedup TTL was 30s but our enforcement read path expects immediate consistency within 5s. So enforcement sometimes sees only the project_tile (triggers 429) while dashboard's org-sum picks up both tiles later (so dashboard shows higher available because org-level accounting spreads differently). Conversely, some cases show dashboard lower than enforcement because dashboard dedup missed and double-counted. TL;DR: shard alignment + dedup TTL + retry path = inconsistent counts between enforcement and dashboard.

kevin_eng: repro steps for infra team:
1) Ingest 2k events with same org_id across 30s burst, using client retries (simulate partial timeout).
2) Verify tile_writer produced both project and org tiles in different shard buckets.
3) Query enforcement path (reads project tiles) and dashboard path (sums project+org) for same time window and compare.

Example curl to reproduce token writes:
```
for i in {1..2000}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/ingest -H "x-org-id: acme" -H "x-project-id: prod" -d '{"tokens":25}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
```

olivia_billing: mitigation for customer?

maria_support: told customer short-term: add a small backoff (reduce burst concurrency) and we can enable temporary per-org soft-limit raise while we fix. They accepted.

kevin_eng: proposed fixes:
- Align shard keys at tile write so org-aggregation uses the same tile set enforcement reads (prefer single canonical tile set per event).
- Reduce dedup TTL from 30s -> 5s and make ingestion idempotent so retries don't create duplicate tiles.
- Add a dashboard-side dedupe step during org-aggregation to ignore tiles already counted by enforcement (fast path).
- Add e2e test that simulates retries + bursts to assert counts match enforcement read.

anna_analytics: will run a backfill job to recompute tiles for the 09:00-09:10 window for Acme to correct dashboard for historical view.

kevin_eng: assigned follow-ups: eng-infra to change dedup TTL + idempotency (P0), eng-runtime to add canonical tile mapping (P1), analytics to run backfill and add reconciliation job (P1).

ryan_pm: I'll draft customer-facing postmortem and rollback plan. Also want to add a dashboard banner when org vs project aggregation may lag.

maria_support: customer update sent: temporary soft-limit + request to throttle bursts. they want ETA.

kevin_eng: ETA for patch = 3 business days for TTL fix and idempotency changes, 2 weeks for full tile canonicalization + e2e tests.

maria_support: thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated and follow up with Acme once TTL patch is deployed. :thumbsup:
